report.summary: Reviewed chunk 4 of daedalus/mapping/inventory.py (lines 841-end): refresh(), check(), _by_key(), _statuses(), _describe_drift(), render_text(), main(). All docstring claims check out against the code shown.

handoff.purpose: Inspect the final chunk of the inventory module: refresh, gate-mode check, drift detection, text rendering, and CLI entry.

symbols.name: refresh
symbols.note: Builds a fresh doc and writes it to the target path; returns a dict with path, doc, and harvest stats. Writes the inventory file.

symbols.name: check
symbols.note: Gate-mode validation: loads the stored inventory, checks schema, digest, annotation overreach, and drift against a fresh build. Returns a dict with ok, path, problems, stored, fresh. Does not write.

symbols.name: _by_key
symbols.note: Extracts each feature's derived half (excluding human fields) keyed by module or by detector:reason for module-less entries. Used for field-level drift.

symbols.name: _statuses
symbols.note: Returns a dict mapping feature keys to their status strings, based on _by_key().

symbols.name: _describe_drift
symbols.note: Compares stored vs fresh docs and produces a list of human-readable drift messages, covering HEAD changes, feature additions/removals/status changes, block changes, and field-level changes.

symbols.name: render_text
symbols.note: Renders a plain-text summary of the doc: schema, repo state, counts, and human annotation counts.

symbols.name: main
symbols.note: CLI entry point. Parses arguments and dispatches to --check, --json, or --refresh. Can write the inventory file when refreshing; otherwise prints output. Exits with 0 or 1.

claims.text: Gate mode. Writes nothing; returns {"ok": bool, "problems": [...]}.
claims.why: The function never calls write_inventory or any file-writing operation; it returns a dict with 'ok' and 'problems' keys, both present in the return statement.

claims.text: Four ways to fail, in the order a reader needs them: 1. there is no inventory, or it cannot be parsed;
claims.why: The function first calls load(target); if stored is None, returns a failure with 'no inventory at ...'. If stored.get('__error__'), returns a failure with 'could not be parsed'.

claims.text: 2. it was written by a different schema;
claims.why: After the parse checks, the code checks if stored.get('schema') != SCHEMA and returns a failure with a schema mismatch message.

claims.text: 3. its digest does not cover its own derived fields -- somebody edited the mechanical half by hand;
claims.why: The code calls digest_ok(stored); if false, it appends a problem message about hand-edited derived fields.

claims.text: 4. regenerating it now would change something -- it is STALE, and the diff says exactly how.
claims.why: The code builds a fresh doc and compares _strip_human(stored) vs _strip_human(fresh); if different, extends problems with _describe_drift(stored, fresh), which produces detailed messages.

claims.text: Every feature's DERIVED half, keyed by module (or by detector for the module-less stale entries). The human fields are dropped so a note cannot read as drift.
claims.why: The function iterates all areas and features, builds a key from module or from detector:reason, and filters out FEATURE_HUMAN_FIELDS from each feature dict. Human fields are excluded.

claims.text: Field-level, not just status-level. A module whose importers or reaching entry point changed is a real difference, and reporting it as "something differs, go diff the file yourself" is how a gate stops being read.
claims.why: The code compares _by_key(stored) vs _by_key(fresh) and lists the specific fields that changed for each shared key, excluding 'status'.

claims.text: Mechanical fields are rewritten every run; human notes are carried forward and excluded from the digest.
claims.why: The refresh function (seen in this chunk) calls build and write_inventory, and the check function uses _strip_human to compare only mechanical fields. The harvest function (defined elsewhere) carries forward annotations. The digest exclusion is implemented in digest_ok (elsewhere), but the description's claim about mechanical rewrite and human carry-forward is consistent with the code shown.

claims.text: gate mode: exit non-zero if the file is missing, hand-edited or stale; writes nothing
claims.why: When --check is set, main calls check(root, target, probe_dirty=probe). If not ok, prints problems and returns 1. The check function writes nothing.

claims.text: print the generated document; writes nothing
claims.why: In the --json branch, the code builds a doc and prints json.dumps(doc, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False). No file write occurs.
The code sets probe = not args.no_git and passes probe_dirty=probe to check() and refresh(). If --no-git is given, probe is False.

observations.what: The check function returns both 'stored' and 'fresh' docs, which could be large; the CLI ignores them, but they are present in the return dict.

In main(), the --json branch calls harvest with old = load(target) or {}; if the file is missing, old is an empty dict, and harvest may behave differently. This is consistent with the help text but could be surprising.

The drift description for field-level changes is truncated to the first 10 entries and then summarized with '... and N more modules'. This could hide details in large inventories, but the summary is explicit.
